structured_output.scope_summary: This revision of EIP-3855 adds the instruction PUSH0 at opcode 0x5f, starting at a fork block HF. PUSH0 has no immediate data and pops nothing. It pushes the constant 0 onto the stack and costs a fixed 2 gas, which the text labels "verylow". The listed test cases cover a single PUSH0, 1024 consecutive PUSH0s (succeeds) and 1025 (stack overflow). The Security Considerations section says jumpdest analysis is unaffected because there is no immediate data. Already-deployed code containing 0x5f may behave differently after the fork.

evidence.locator: Specification — "The cost of this instruction is 2 gas (aka `verylow`)"
evidence.summary: The new instruction uses a constant cost from an existing gas tier. No accounting rule changes.

evm_gas_rule_changes.rationale: A new instruction priced at an existing constant tier is not a new accounting mechanism, and it does not change any existing gas rule or baseline expectation.
evm_gas_rule_changes.uncertainty_note: The tier name conflicts with the number 2 (see UNSP). Either way it is a constant from an existing tier, so this score is unaffected.

evidence.locator: Specification — "pops no items from the stack, and places a single item with the value 0"
evidence.summary: PUSH0 only touches the stack and does not access state.

state_access_ordering_within_opcode_exec.rationale: No state access occurs, and no ordering rule changes.

evidence.summary: Only an EVM instruction is specified. Blob gas is not mentioned.
There is no state-writing or state-gas rule.
No refund is defined.

new_evm_gas_refund.rationale: No new refund mechanism is introduced.

evidence.locator: Backwards Compatibility — "Already deployed contracts using this opcode could change their behaviour"
evidence.summary: Before the fork, 0x5f is undefined. Baseline tests that expect it to abort as an invalid opcode must change.

patterns_affecting_pre_existing_tests.rationale: Rework is limited to the one parameter value 0x5f within the undefined/invalid-opcode test family. That is localized rework in one behavioral family.
patterns_affecting_pre_existing_tests.uncertainty_note: How much rework is needed depends on whether baseline invalid-opcode tests enumerate 0x5f. No test suite was supplied.

evidence.summary: No new log, header, receipt or other output is produced.

new_invariant_on_pre_existing_tests.rationale: Baseline tests need no new assertion.

evidence.summary: Only an EVM instruction changes. No t8n inputs or outputs are affected.

transition_tool_interface_changes.rationale: The tool interface does not change. Fork selection covers the new behavior.

evidence.summary: The tests are plain bytecode with stack, success and stack-overflow expectations.

new_test_framework_primitives.rationale: Baseline primitives (bytecode, stack-overflow and gas expectations) are enough. Adding a PUSH0 mnemonic to the opcode list is a new value, not a new abstraction.
new_test_framework_primitives.uncertainty_note: One could argue the opcode list needs a local extension (level 1).

evidence.summary: No cryptography is involved.

evidence.locator: Test Cases — "(1025 times) -- execution aborts due to out of stack"
evidence.summary: The outcome flips at the 1024-item stack limit for the new instruction.
Whether 0x5f is valid depends on the fork boundary.

edge_boundary_conditions.rationale: There is one boundary-sensitive mechanism: the new push instruction's validity and stack-limit behavior, plus fork activation and exact gas or out-of-gas. There is no elevated matrix.
edge_boundary_conditions.uncertainty_note: The stack limit itself is an existing rule. Someone could argue for 0, but the new instruction's own overflow behavior needs boundary cases.

evidence.summary: No block-structure or RLP validation rules change.
The Engine API is not involved.

engine_api_changes.rationale: The Engine API does not change.

evidence.summary: No system contract is introduced.
No system contract is affected.

evidence.locator: Specification — "It has no immediate data, pops no items from the stack, and places a single item"
evidence.summary: One new instruction with no immediate data, fixed stack effects and constant gas.

added_opcodes.rationale: Exactly one simple instruction is introduced.

evidence.summary: Changing other instructions is given only as motivation. No existing instruction's semantics are modified.

modified_opcodes.rationale: 0x5f was previously undefined. Defining it counts as an added opcode, not a modification of an existing one.

evidence.summary: No precompile is added.
No precompile is changed.
No serialized schema changes.
No transaction type is introduced.
No transaction-validity or intrinsic-gas changes.
No header fields are added.
Activation only selects which rules apply. There is no state migration.

new_fork_activation_mechanism.rationale: No activation-specific state transition is needed.

evidence.summary: A trivial constant push priced like other constant-pushing instructions.

performance_risks.rationale: No additional performance-validation requirement is established.

evidence.locator: Security Considerations — "jumpdest-analysis is unaffected, as `PUSH0` has no immediate data bytes"
evidence.summary: Jumpdest analysis must not treat 0x5f as having immediate data.
Deployed code containing 0x5f changes behavior from aborting to succeeding.

security_risks.rationale: The security conditions (jumpdest analysis does not skip bytes after 0x5f, and pre-fork vs post-fork validity) can be checked locally.

evidence.locator: Specification — "The cost of this instruction is 2 gas (aka `verylow`)"
evidence.summary: In standard gas-tier naming, 2 gas is the base tier, while verylow is 3 gas. The label conflicts with the number.
The instructions cited as comparisons cost 2 gas, which supports the explicit value of 2.

unspecified_behavior_requiring_cross_cli.rationale: The tier label is inconsistent, but the explicit number and the comparison instructions point to one intended outcome: 2 gas. That makes this a localized omission or detail at level 1.
unspecified_behavior_requiring_cross_cli.uncertainty_note: If an implementer followed the tier name, gas results would differ (3 vs 2). That reading could justify level 2.

evidence.locator: Motivation — "This was proposed as a way to chain transactions (i.e. EIP-2733)"
evidence.summary: EIP-2733 is cited only as motivation for not depending on RETURNDATASIZE being zero. PUSH0 does not interact with its behavior.

cross_eip_interactions.rationale: PUSH0 behaves the same regardless of any other EIP. The EIP-2733 citation is motivation only.

under_specification.summary: The gas cost says "2 gas (aka verylow)". In conventional tier naming, verylow is 3 gas and 2 gas is the base tier. The explicit number and the comparison to ADDRESS and ORIGIN support 2 gas.
unresolved_questions: Is the intended cost 2 gas (the explicit number) or the verylow tier value (3 gas)?
The fork is identified only as an HF block number.

notable_ambiguities: The "verylow" label conflicts with the stated 2-gas cost. The cited comparison instructions (ADDRESS, ORIGIN) cost 2, which suggests the label is wrong rather than the number.
Activation is given as BLOCK_NUMBER >= HF, with no concrete fork block.
